nodes.label: React Native Dev
nodes.rationale: Build the screen correctly first, and measure before changing anything that is slow. Web-only React goes to frontend-developer. APIs and servers go to backend-developer.

nodes.label: React Native
nodes.source_location: Step 0 — Orient in the project (always, ~2 minutes)
nodes.rationale: React Native 0.76 and newer enables the New Architecture by default, and Hermes is the default engine. Check versions before recommending an API.

nodes.label: Expo
nodes.source_location: Step 0 — Orient in the project (always, ~2 minutes)
nodes.rationale: Read the Expo SDK version from the mobile package.json, and read app.json, babel, Metro, and eas.json before writing code.

nodes.label: Hermes
nodes.source_location: Step 0 — Orient in the project (always, ~2 minutes)
nodes.rationale: Hermes is the default JS engine. Dev mode with the debugger and no minification can be 5 to 10 times slower, so profile a release-like build.

nodes.label: New Architecture
nodes.source_location: Step 0 — Orient in the project (always, ~2 minutes)
nodes.rationale: On by default at React Native 0.76 or newer. FlashList v2 requires it, and some libraries behave differently, so check the flag before recommending an API.

nodes.label: FlashList
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Use FlashList when it is installed for any list that can exceed about 20 rows. It needs size hints. Version 2 requires the New Architecture. Adding it as a new native dependency needs a dev-client or EAS build, not a reload.

nodes.label: FlatList
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: A tuned FlatList is the fallback when FlashList is not installed. Use a stable keyExtractor, a memoized renderItem and row, no inline object or function props, and getItemLayout when heights are known.

nodes.label: ScrollView
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Do not render dynamic data with ScrollView plus map. Lists are where these apps get janky.

nodes.label: Reanimated
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Animate on the UI thread with Reanimated worklets or useNativeDriver. Animate transform and opacity, not width, height, top, or left. Avoid setState once per frame.

nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Check whether React Compiler is enabled before hand-memoizing. Memoization costs memory and complexity.

nodes.label: expo-image
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Use expo-image or FastImage with explicit dimensions, caching, placeholders, and correctly sized sources. Do not ship a 4000px image into an 80px avatar.

nodes.label: FastImage
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: FastImage is the named alternative to expo-image for sized, cached images.

nodes.label: InteractionManager
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Move heavy JS off the touch path with InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions, chunking, or a worker or native module. Also defer non-critical startup until after the first render.

nodes.label: Metro
nodes.source_location: Step 0 — Orient in the project (always, ~2 minutes)
nodes.rationale: Metro config carries inlineRequires, custom resolvers, and polyfills. A native dependency still needs a new build rather than a Metro reload.

nodes.label: inlineRequires
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Keep the root lean by lazy-requiring heavy screens and modules with Metro inlineRequires, and defer analytics and wallet or network warm-up until after first render.

nodes.label: expo-secure-store
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Keys, seeds, and tokens go in expo-secure-store, Keychain, or Keystore. Never AsyncStorage or logs. Strip console.log in production.

nodes.label: AsyncStorage
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Do not store secrets in AsyncStorage. It is the slower non-sensitive option compared with MMKV.

nodes.label: EAS
nodes.source_location: Step 1 — Classify the request
nodes.rationale: Build, release, and native-dependency changes go through EAS or a dev client. A reload is not enough when native code changes.

nodes.label: JS thread
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: The JS thread has about 16ms at 60fps or 8ms at 120fps. It is a bottleneck when too many renders, heavy computation, or bridge and JSI chatter keep it busy, which blocks touch handling and animations.

nodes.label: UI thread
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: UI-thread bottlenecks are overdraw, huge views, shadows, non-native animations, and big images. The frame budget is about 16ms at 60fps or 8ms at 120fps.

nodes.label: Startup
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: Startup cost is bundle size, eager imports, and blocking init. Keep the splash up only until the first meaningful frame, not longer.

nodes.label: Memory
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: Memory bottlenecks are leaks, unbounded caches, and large images or lists. Every subscription, timer, and AppState, NetInfo, or event listener needs a useEffect cleanup. Leaks show up as slow degradation after navigating back and forth.

nodes.label: Network and IO
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: Network bottlenecks are waterfall requests, missing caches, large payloads, and synchronous storage. Assume flaky connectivity: timeouts, backoff, AbortController cancellation, optimistic UI where it is safe, and a visible offline state.

nodes.label: apps/mobile/src/_legacy
nodes.source_location: Rule — `src/_legacy` is off-limits unless the user says so
nodes.rationale: Holds the old mobile backend, Stellar, storage, and auth logic as reference only. Do not edit or import it from live code. It is excluded from tsconfig.json. Build the frontend against mock data unless the user explicitly asks to use it, and then copy the needed logic out rather than importing across the boundary.

nodes.label: apps/mobile
nodes.rationale: This skill applies when the work is in the Expo app at apps/mobile, including screens, Metro, babel, app.json, and eas.json.

nodes.label: AbortController
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Cancel or dedupe in-flight requests on unmount so a slow network does not update an unmounted screen.

nodes.label: React.memo
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: Use React.memo only on components that receive stable props and render often. useCallback and useMemo belong where they feed a memoized child or an expensive computation, not on every function.

nodes.label: backend-developer
nodes.rationale: API and server work is deferred to the backend-developer skill.

nodes.label: NetInfo
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: NetInfo listeners need cleanup. Connectivity should be treated as flaky, with a visible offline or degraded state.

nodes.label: AppState
nodes.source_location: Building — principles that prevent most performance bugs
nodes.rationale: AppState listeners need a useEffect cleanup. Low-RAM Android devices can kill the app in the background.

nodes.label: Flipper
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: Hermes profiles can be captured from Flipper or the newer React Native DevTools when a device profiler is available.

nodes.label: React DevTools Profiler
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: Use the profiler and Highlight updates to find render cost before changing code. If no device is available, say the diagnosis is static, not measured.

nodes.label: Perf Monitor
nodes.source_location: Performance workflow — measure, then fix
nodes.rationale: The Perf Monitor overlay is the named way to separate JS-thread and UI-thread frame drops.
